notices.agency_name: New York City Police Pension Fund
notices.short_title: Virtual Chief Information Security Officer (vCISO) Services
notices.description: The New York City Police Pension Fund is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide Virtual Chief Information Security Officer (vCISO) services. The selected firm will support the Fund in enhancing and maturing its cybersecurity program; strengthening cybersecurity governance, oversight, and accountability; improving cybersecurity risk visibility through metrics, reporting, and dashboards; enhancing incident preparedness, response, and recovery capabilities; and aligning cybersecurity practices with applicable New York City policies, standards, and fiduciary obligations. Additional information is provided in the RFP.
notices.plain: The New York City Police Pension Fund is seeking competing proposals from qualified firms to provide virtual chief information security officer services to help strengthen its cybersecurity program, with responses due Sept. 17, 2026.

notices.description: Sole Source contract for maintenance & upgrades to NYPD's Intelligence Database System (IDS). The Intelligence Database System is a case management system used as the central repository for all NYPD counterterrorism leads, confidential informant credentials and sensitive investigation data. General Dynamics Information Technology Inc. is the sole manufacturer and provider of Intelligence Database System software and Intelligence Bureau Intranet support services.
notices.plain: The New York Police Department awarded General Dynamics Information Technology Inc. a $1,390,319 sole-source contract, meaning no other vendor was considered, to maintain and upgrade its Intelligence Database System, the case management system holding counterterrorism leads and sensitive investigation data.

notices.short_title: FY27 QUEENS EAST INDUSTRIAL BUSINESS SOLUTIONS PROGRAM (ISBP) NAE
notices.description:
The NYC Department of Small Business Services is entering into a negotiated acquisition extension contract with Chamber of Commerce Borough of Queens to support the industrial and manufacturing sector by responding to current and evolving needs while providing the conditions and resources to enable the sector to further grow and advance. The contract term will be from 7/1/2026 to 6/30/2027, in the amount of $170,000.00.

The negotiated acquisition extension will allow the agency adequate time to release a new solicitation for this program and enable the current IBSP provider to continue to deliver a suite of business services not limited to boro-wide technical consultant services, accessing incentive programs, providing information regarding City, State and Federal programs.

Vendors interested in responding to this or other future solicitations for these types of services should contact Kelly Taylor at Procurementhelpdesk@sbs.nyc.gov.
notices.plain: The Department of Small Business Services plans to extend its contract with the Chamber of Commerce Borough of Queens for $170,000 to keep running the Queens East industrial business solutions program from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, while it prepares a new solicitation.

notices.short_title: COMPASS Center Based  Queens 02 Middle School
notices.description: COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs.

notices.description: DYCD plans to extend their Immigrant Families contracts. These providers deliver comprehensive services for immigrant families living in low income neighborhoods throughout the city of New York. The goal of the comprehensive services to immigrant families is to: Identify the complex and multiple needs of newly-arrived limited English proficiency families, and, in collaboration with a network of community-based providers, ensure that they gain access to services that help them become self-sufficient and prosper. Help each enrolled family build the self-advocacy skills and gain the knowledge to enable them to address specific challenges and navigate key systems that impact their lives (for example, the education, healthcare, housing, benefits, tax, workplace, and legal and immigration systems).
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Queens Community House Inc. a $348,593 negotiated contract, without open competition, to provide comprehensive services for low-income immigrant families, including help navigating systems such as education, housing and immigration.
